shared_context: Consumer query: definition and overview of blepharitis (eyelid inflammation)

atoms.1: Blepharitis is an inflammation of the eyelids.
atoms.2: Blepharitis typically involves the part of the eyelid where the eyelashes grow.
atoms.3: Blepharitis can cause symptoms such as itching.
atoms.4: Blepharitis can cause symptoms such as redness.
atoms.5: Blepharitis can cause symptoms such as swelling.
atoms.6: Blepharitis can cause symptoms such as crusting around the eyelashes.
atoms.7: Blepharitis is often a chronic condition.
atoms.8: Blepharitis can be challenging to manage.
atoms.9: There are two main types of blepharitis: anterior and posterior.
atoms.10: Anterior blepharitis affects the outside front edge of the eyelid where the eyelashes are attached.
atoms.11: Posterior blepharitis affects the inner edge of the eyelid that comes into contact with the eyeball.
atoms.12: Posterior blepharitis is often associated with dysfunction of the meibomian glands.
atoms.13: Common causes of blepharitis include bacterial infections.
atoms.14: Common causes of blepharitis include infections by Staphylococcus species.
atoms.15: Common causes of blepharitis include skin conditions such as seborrheic dermatitis.
atoms.16: Common causes of blepharitis include skin conditions such as rosacea.
atoms.17: Other contributing factors to blepharitis can include allergies.
atoms.18: Other contributing factors to blepharitis can include eyelash mites (Demodex).
atoms.19: Other contributing factors to blepharitis can include poor eyelid hygiene.
atoms.20: Treatment for blepharitis typically involves maintaining good eyelid hygiene.
atoms.21: Good eyelid hygiene includes regular cleaning of the eyelid margins with warm compresses.
atoms.22: Good eyelid hygiene includes regular cleaning of the eyelid margins with diluted baby shampoo.
atoms.23: Good eyelid hygiene includes regular cleaning of the eyelid margins with commercial lid scrubs.
atoms.24: In some cases, topical antibiotics may be prescribed to manage bacterial infections in blepharitis.
atoms.25: In some cases, oral antibiotics may be prescribed to manage bacterial infections in blepharitis.
atoms.26: Managing underlying conditions like seborrheic dermatitis can help control symptoms of blepharitis.
atoms.27: Managing underlying conditions like rosacea can help control symptoms of blepharitis.

snippets.output: Blepharitis is an inflammation of the eyelids, typically involving the part of the eyelid where the eyelashes grow.
Blepharitis can cause symptoms such as itching, redness, swelling, and crusting around the eyelashes.
Blepharitis is often a chronic condition that can be challenging to manage.

There are two main types of blepharitis: anterior and posterior. Anterior blepharitis affects the outside front edge of the eyelid where the eyelashes are attached, while posterior blepharitis affects the inner edge of the eyelid that contacts the eyeball and is often associated with dysfunction of the meibomian glands.
